newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee stays lower by close, origins seen.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee stays lower by close, origins seen.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures kept early losses up to the close as aggressive hedge selling by the origins met with very little roaster buying interest.
"London came off on selling pressure from the origins. The arb (arbitrage) widens as New York goes up and London actually comes off a little bit," said one trader.
But robusta's downside was supported by some scale-down manufacturer buying at the lows.
Traders said front-month November was $17 down on the day to close at $1,495 a tonne. The contract was due $20 at the opening and it hovered around that level for most part of the day.

Other positions were $14 to $24 lower. Volume on the exchange reached 3,305 lots. In structure, both nearby Nov/Jan and Jan/March spread remained firm. The Nov/Jan spread was seen widening up to $72 at one stage before finishing at $69.
Interest was also seen in options, with activity focusing on March $1,450 and $1,650 calls.
Traders said good physical demand for robusta coffee, possibly to fill the arabica supply gap, could help provide a near-term support for the coffee.
"There has been good robusta interest in the U.S. and the Far East for next year...there has been aggressive buying by the industry," said one trader.
On the physical front, the market is also keeping a close tab on Central and South American arabica coffee sales in the coming weeks.
"Brazil has certainly been an active (seller) recently, but the pressure to off-load coffee at current prices is not huge," broker GNI said in daily commentary.
Brazilians went to the polls on Thursday to elect major and councilmen for 5,500 cities. Thursday has been declared a national holiday.
In other news, the International Coffee Organisation said exporting members exports fell to 5.46 million 60-kg bags in August from 5.79 million in July and 5.92 million in August 1995.
